claim_boundary: Controlled deterministic Track A comparison of a frozen reject-aware sentinel policy with the closed identity policy. No external validation, learned ontology formation, necessary revision, semantic novelty, sealed transfer, statistical population inference, comparative superiority, real ARC intervention, or Track B claim.

development_selection.data_status: completed and fully opened Track A 006a outcome
development_selection.rule: Select the smallest tested sentinel count tied for the largest observed outside-detection count.

execution.heldout_target_information: Neither policy receives the target transitions, hash, kind, generation seed, or execution observations before action selection.

policies.closed_identity_native: Unchanged exact minimum-worst-case identity policy over four base candidates, executed at its own certified depth.
policies.reject_aware_equal_closed_horizon: The frozen reject-aware policy truncated at the closed identity policy's certified depth; nonterminal truncation is unresolved.
policies.reject_aware_native: Exact minimum-worst-case policy over four bases plus two sentinels under the frozen reject-aware terminal rule, executed at its own certified depth.

acceptance: four bases are globally behaviorally distinct and have an exact closed identity depth from 2 through 6
two sentinels are globally behaviorally distinct from every base and each other
reject-aware synthesis is exact and solved with certified depth no greater than 8
the held-out outside target is globally behaviorally distinct from all four bases and both sentinels
generation.first_observation_rule: Every action from initial state s0 emits o0; information can appear only after a hidden state transition.
generation.namespace_separation: base, sentinel, and outside machines use distinct SHA-256-framed stage labels under the held-out master seed

primary: paired native-depth outside detection counts for closed identity and reject-aware policies
paired native-depth false candidate identification counts for closed identity and reject-aware policies
outcomes.required_soundness: Both native policies must correctly identify all 256 in-family targets. Any incorrect identification or reject is an instrument blocker.
secondary: reject-aware equal-closed-horizon outside detection, false identification, and unresolved counts
reject-aware equal-closed-horizon in-family correct, incorrect, reject, and unresolved counts
policy depth, root-action, reachable-belief, generation-attempt, rejection, and trace accounting
outcomes.statistics: Exact deterministic paired corpus counts only; no p-values, confidence intervals, population generalization, or superiority claim.

prospective_ordering: two-sentinel configuration selected only from opened 006a development cases
held-out generator, seed, filters, terminal rule, policies, horizons, endpoints, and evidence format frozen
freeze merged before held-out case generation
future single held-out execution and immutable outcome packaging

reject_aware_terminal_rule.identify: exactly one base candidate and no sentinel survives
reject_aware_terminal_rule.nonterminal: one or more bases survive together with a sentinel, or two or more bases survive
reject_aware_terminal_rule.reject: no base candidate survives, regardless of how many sentinels survive

stop_rules: Stop with a generation blocker if any stage exhausts 2000 attempts.
Stop with an instrument blocker if either accepted native policy is not exact and solved.
Stop with an instrument blocker if either native policy incorrectly identifies or rejects any in-family target.
Do not change configuration, seed, filters, terminal rule, horizons, endpoints, or evidence format after held-out execution; defects require a new numbered slice.
